views.name: patient_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ID,
  SEX,
  Birthday,
  Description,
  "First Date",
  Admission,
  Diagnosis
FROM Patient
views.description: One row per patient with core demographic and administrative attributes. Use as the patient-level backbone to join to event tables or to filter cohorts. | Use for: list patients with demographic attributes; join patient attributes to laboratories or examinations; filter cohorts by SEX, Admission, or patient-level Diagnosis

views.name: examination_events
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ID,
  "Examination Date",
  "aCL IgG",
  "aCL IgM",
  ANA,
  "ANA Pattern",
  "aCL IgA",
  Diagnosis,
  KCT,
  RVVT,
  LAC,
  Symptoms,
  Thrombosis
FROM Examination
views.description: One row per Examination record (patient exam event) exposing test results and clinical flags. Use to count exams, filter by test flags, or join to patient or laboratory events. | Use for: count exams per patient or time window; identify exams with positive antibody flags (KCT/RVVT/LAC); study associations between exam findings and diagnoses or thrombosis

views.description: One row per Laboratory measurement event for each patient-date with the full set of lab measurements and qualitative flags. Use for time-series analysis, aggregations, or to join to examinations. | Use for: compute per-patient summary statistics of lab measures; retrieve labs within date ranges; join labs to exam events on patient and date

views.name: latest_examination_per_patient
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.ID,
  e."Examination Date",
  e."aCL IgG",
  e."aCL IgM",
  e.ANA,
  e."ANA Pattern",
  e."aCL IgA",
  e.Diagnosis,
  e.KCT,
  e.RVVT,
  e.LAC,
  e.Symptoms,
  e.Thrombosis
FROM Examination e
INNER JOIN (
  SELECT
    ID,
    MAX("Examination Date") AS max_exam_date
  FROM Examination
  GROUP BY ID
) mx ON e.ID = mx.ID AND e."Examination Date" = mx.max_exam_date
views.description: Latest Examination row per patient based on Examination Date. Useful to attach the most recent exam result or diagnosis to a patient profile. | Use for: attach latest exam diagnosis or antibody status to each patient; compare latest exam to latest labs; cohort selection based on most recent exam attributes

views.name: latest_lab_per_patient
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  l.ID,
  l.Date,
  l.GOT,
  l.GPT,
  l.LDH,
  l.ALP,
  l.TP,
  l.ALB,
  l.UA,
  l.UN,
  l.CRE,
  l."T-BIL",
  l."T-CHO",
  l.TG,
  l.CPK,
  l.GLU,
  l.WBC,
  l.RBC,
  l.HGB,
  l.HCT,
  l.PLT,
  l.PT,
  l.APTT,
  l.FG,
  l.PIC,
  l.TAT,
  l.TAT2,
  l."U-PRO",
  l.IGG,
  l.IGA,
  l.IGM,
  l.CRP,
  l.RA,
  l.RF,
  l.C3,
  l.C4,
  l.RNP,
  l.SM,
  l.SC170,
  l.SSA,
  l.SSB,
  l.CENTROMEA,
  l.DNA,
  l."DNA-II"
FROM Laboratory l
INNER JOIN (
  SELECT
    ID,
    MAX(Date) AS max_date
  FROM Laboratory
  GROUP BY ID
) mx ON l.ID = mx.ID AND l.Date = mx.max_date
views.description: Latest Laboratory measurement row per patient (by Date). Use to obtain the most recent lab values per patient for cross-sectional analyses or to join to patient/exam latest snapshots. | Use for: cross-sectional analyses using most recent lab values per patient; merge latest labs with patient demographics or latest exam

views.name: per_patient_lab_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ID,
  COUNT(*) AS lab_record_count,
  MIN(Date) AS lab_first_date,
  MAX(Date) AS lab_last_date,
  AVG(CAST(HGB AS REAL)) AS avg_HGB,
  MAX(HGB) AS max_HGB,
  AVG(CAST(CRE AS REAL)) AS avg_CRE,
  MAX(CRE) AS max_CRE,
  AVG(CAST(WBC AS REAL)) AS avg_WBC,
  MAX(WBC) AS max_WBC
FROM Laboratory
GROUP BY ID
views.description: Per-patient aggregated summary statistics (count, first date, last date, average and max) for common numeric lab measures. Useful for longitudinal summaries and cohort filters based on historical lab exposure. | Use for: identify patients with many or recent lab tests; filter patients by average or max lab values (HGB, CRE, WBC); describe lab measurement density per patient

views.name: patient_exam_lab_snapshot
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.ID,
  p.SEX,
  p.Birthday,
  p.Description,
  p."First Date",
  p.Admission,
  p.Diagnosis AS "Patient Diagnosis",
  e."Examination Date",
  e.Diagnosis AS "Exam Diagnosis",
  e.KCT,
  e.RVVT,
  e.LAC,
  l.Date AS "Lab Date",
  l.CRE
FROM Patient p
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT e1.*
  FROM Examination e1
  INNER JOIN (
    SELECT ID, MAX("Examination Date") AS max_exam_date FROM Examination GROUP BY ID
  ) em ON e1.ID = em.ID AND e1."Examination Date" = em.max_exam_date
) e ON p.ID = e.ID
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT l1.*
  FROM Laboratory l1
  INNER JOIN (
    SELECT ID, MAX(Date) AS max_date FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID
  ) lm ON l1.ID = lm.ID AND l1.Date = lm.max_date
) l ON p.ID = l.ID
views.description: Denormalized snapshot joining patient, latest examination, and latest laboratory per patient. Useful for cross-sectional patient profiles combining demographics, most recent exam, and most recent lab values. | Use for: build patient profile combining demographics + latest exam + latest lab; compare patient-level diagnosis to most recent exam diagnosis or creatinine; select cohorts based on combined snapshot attributes

views.name: examination_antibody_flags
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ID,
  "Examination Date",
  KCT,
  RVVT,
  LAC,
  CASE WHEN KCT IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(KCT) <> '-' AND TRIM(KCT) <> '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS KCT_positive,
  CASE WHEN RVVT IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(RVVT) <> '-' AND TRIM(RVVT) <> '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS RVVT_positive,
  CASE WHEN LAC IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(LAC) <> '-' AND TRIM(LAC) <> '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS LAC_positive
FROM Examination
views.description: Normalized boolean-style flags derived from Examination KCT, RVVT, LAC text fields. Exposes canonicalized binary indicators (0/1) for positive-like tokens. Use when testing for positive antibody tests in queries. NOTE: semantic_filters should declare which tokens are considered 'positive' for downstream use. | Use for: count positive antibody tests per patient; filter exams by any positive coagulation antibody; study relation of positive flags to thrombosis

views.name: patient_age_at_latest_lab
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.ID,
  p.Birthday,
  l.Date AS lab_date,
  (CAST(strftime('%Y', l.Date) AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%Y', p.Birthday) AS INTEGER)
    - CASE WHEN strftime('%m-%d', l.Date) < strftime('%m-%d', p.Birthday) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
  ) AS age_at_latest_lab
FROM Patient p
INNER JOIN (
  SELECT l1.*
  FROM Laboratory l1
  INNER JOIN (
    SELECT ID, MAX(Date) AS max_date FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID
  ) lm ON l1.ID = lm.ID AND l1.Date = lm.max_date
) l ON p.ID = l.ID
views.description: Compute patient age (in years, approximate using date difference) at the time of their latest Laboratory Date. Useful for analyses stratified by age at most recent labs. | Use for: age-stratified summaries using age at last lab; filter patients by age at last lab measurement
